cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, and the direction is genuinely yours.
cells.act: find the rhythm and stay in it
cells.ask: Notice this week which pace of work you could keep for a month, and choose that speed once or twice, deliberately, even when a faster one is possible.
cells.core:
What you're drawn to is being followed at the pace of the want itself. Not the speed you'd keep for a day, the speed you'd keep for a month. When those two match, the work doesn't arrive with a lurch; it accumulates, and you can feel it accumulating. You recognize this in yourself already, which is why the days when it's running well feel less like effort and more like arriving somewhere you were already headed.

The place this gets tested is the start. There's usually a stretch where the honest rhythm is slower than the excitement suggests, and the cleanest move isn't to push through but to let the slow pace carry the day. The will and the doing go the same way. Try it once and see.
cells.sheetLine: The same will and the same wanting, moving at the same speed.
cells.verb: To feel something imagined all the way through until the satisfaction of it arrives.
cells.place: Standing with a light out ahead you recognize and want to move toward.

cells.tense: You will have it finished, certain, and proven before you let it begin.
cells.ask: Pick something you're tending that has a life of its own, and give it a day with your hands off — then look at it the morning after.
cells.core:
The appetite has jumped ahead of what's here. In your head the thing is already complete, or already ruined, and the middle where it actually lives keeps getting skipped. So you tend whatever's around you harder than it's asking for. Which isn't neglect. It's the opposite, and it's tiring in a way that leaves nothing over for the thing itself.

You know what tending without force feels like — you've done it for other people. This is the same move on your own work. Stand back from one thing for a day, deliberately. Let the day have it. What's alive there survives the pause; what doesn't wasn't growing anyway. Come back the next morning and look. You'll know which was which.

cells.tense: You stood at the edge of the thing and did not walk through, and some of you is still there.
cells.act: keep the truth a while before saying it
cells.ask: Hold two things you've come to about where you're headed, side by side, without settling which is right and without telling anyone.
cells.core:
The pull is there, you can feel it — but you're at the door with the handle in your hand. Some past moment when it went differently is still holding the light at a distance, and the standing-there has become the habit. The territory is familiar. You're just not in it.

Do less, not more. Every thing you've settled about the direction is used to make you start moving, and the pushing hasn't worked. Instead, keep two things you've come to — one that argues for the light and one that qualifies it — without settling which is right and without saying either to anyone. Held so, without a verdict, they gather what they need. Some shifted morning one of them will lean. Move then.

cells.tense: You are already moving toward something and you tell the room you were only looking.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Jot down the few things you actually reach for — not what you say you care about, the choices you keep making — and read the pattern back.
cells.core:
You've been treating your own pull like something that just happens, like the body doing the steering without you. Others can see the direction; they've watched you choose. You talk about it as if you happened to be there. The work of paying attention is being done, but you aren't counting it as yours.

Return to the smaller version of this. Before you were following anything impressive, you were simply tracking what you kept returning to. Do that again — keep count of where the choices actually go, not where you'd like them to go, and not what you'd say about them if asked. What's left once you've set the rest down is the light. It was simpler than all this.
